# setfileattr

Sets attributes of a file or directory. *(version 4.69 or later)*

```ttl
setfileattr <filename> <attributes>
```

## Parameters

**string &lt;filename&gt;**

The file name or directory name

**integer &lt;attributes&gt;**

A user can specify a attribute value combined in the following:
Value Meaning $1 Read only $2 Hidden $4 The operating system uses a part of, or uses exclusively $20 Archive $80 Not have other attributes set
Enabled when the value is independently specified. $100 Temporary $1000 Physically moved to offline storage(Windows 2000 or later) $2000 Not to be indexed by the content indexing service(Windows 2000 or later)

## Return Value

**System variable &lt;result&gt;**

When the command fails, 0 is stored.
When the command succeeds, 1 is stored.

## Example

```ttl
; add readonly attribute
file = 'c:\test.txt'
getfileattr file
attr = result | $1 ; keep current attributes
setfileattr file attr
```
